rules.when: approved tasks are stored outside the runtime queue
rules.rule: surface them in the dashboard until a deterministic approval-to-queue bridge exists

rules.when: dashboard controls are simplified
rules.rule: keep mobile-first cards for status, queue, logs, and pending approvals

rules.when: task registry items span multiple states
rules.rule: group them by status and show a single recommended next action

rules.when: task registry items are used across multiple runs
rules.rule: store stable ids and timestamps so future state transitions and audits are deterministic

rules.when: approval actions hand tasks into execution
rules.rule: approve through the same queue safety checks used by manual submissions and append an audit history entry

rules.when: queue execution changes the real state of an approved registry task
rules.rule: mirror the runtime outcome back into tasks.json with deterministic history entries so approved work does not stay stale after execution

rules.when: task board cards need retry and completion context
rules.rule: normalize execution and history fields in the task-registry API before rendering them in the mobile dashboard

rules.when: approved work is recovered directly from a verified working tree
rules.rule: clear stale queue entries and mark the registry task complete in the same change so the loop does not re-run recovered work

rules.when: manual recovery completes approved work outside the queue
rules.rule: append a deterministic manual_recovery record to tasks.log and regenerate metrics.json from the registry snapshot so observability reflects the recovered outcome

rules.when: dashboard task actions mutate tasks.json directly
rules.rule: regenerate codex-learning/metrics.json in the same request path so approval and rejection changes persist between queue runs

rules.when: dashboard APIs are used for status, metrics, or task-registry reads
rules.rule: keep GET paths side-effect free; do not seed follow-up work or mutate tasks.json while serving observability reads

rules.when: the dashboard polls status, metrics, queue, project list, and task registry on a fixed interval
rules.rule: serve the regular UI refresh from one combined snapshot endpoint so polling reduces request churn without changing the deterministic read model

rules.when: dashboard refreshes run on fixed timers while earlier network reads are still in flight
rules.rule: coalesce overlapping browser refresh requests into at most one trailing rerun so slow responses do not stack duplicate poll cycles

rules.when: a combined dashboard snapshot endpoint already loaded shared runtime artifacts
rules.rule: thread preloaded task-registry, external-signal, and strategy snapshot data through downstream readers instead of rereading the same files inside nested status/metrics helpers

rules.when: status responses already have a preloaded task-registry snapshot available
rules.rule: reuse that snapshot when deriving strategy health so `/api/status` does not reread status, queue, registry, and task log on the same request

rules.when: multiple dashboard read endpoints need the same task-registry snapshot, settings, auth, runtime, and external-signal context
rules.rule: build one shared dashboard artifact bundle and hand it to status, metrics, task-registry, and dashboard responses instead of letting each endpoint assemble its own partial preload contract

rules.when: the high-frequency `/api/dashboard` refresh already has task history previews and last-event metadata available
rules.rule: omit the full per-task `history` array from the combined dashboard snapshot and expose only compact history metadata there, so fixed-interval UI refreshes stop re-sending large audit trails that the board does not render

rules.when: the combined `/api/dashboard` snapshot already includes only the task fields rendered by the board
rules.rule: strip non-rendered task metadata such as `execution_brief`, `approval_execution_brief`, and root `task_intent` from the compact dashboard task payload while keeping the full `/api/task-registry` record unchanged

rules.when: the dashboard board already has `active_work` summaries plus `execution` state for live progress rendering
rules.rule: omit raw `failure_context` and full `execution_context.plan_steps` from the compact `/api/dashboard` task payload, and keep only the minimal execution counters needed for fallback rendering while leaving `/api/task-registry` untouched

rules.when: the compact `/api/dashboard` task snapshot already has the handoff summary and only needs approval-shape data for blocked tasks
rules.rule: keep only `queue_handoff.at`, `queue_handoff.task`, and `queue_handoff.status`, and omit `task_shape` entirely unless `approval_ready` is false so fixed-interval board refreshes stop carrying unused handoff intent and approval metadata

rules.when: the dashboard keeps polling while the task-registry file contents are unchanged
rules.rule: cache the normalized task-registry read behind a file-signature check and invalidate it on writes, so repeated dashboard refreshes stop reparsing the same large registry until the file actually changes

rules.when: task-registry pressure is already derived during artifact sync or persisted dashboard refreshes
rules.rule: prefer the aggregated on-disk registry file sizes over reserializing normalized tasks, so pressure metrics reflect the real read surface without extra full-payload work

rules.when: self-improve decides whether to generate a registry-pressure follow-up
rules.rule: reuse the shared `task_registry_pressure_detected` signal and 512KB threshold from persisted metrics instead of maintaining a separate local cutoff, so autonomous task generation follows the same pressure policy as strategy and dashboard metrics

rules.when: retry classification coverage drops below 50% across at least 10 retry records
rules.rule: prioritize a self-improve task that enriches orchestrator failure capture and classify_failure patterns before broader retry tuning, so future task selection is based on trustworthy failure categories

rules.when: zero-step timeout pressure is high and diagnostic_coverage drops below 35% across at least 20 failure records
rules.rule: prioritize a self-improve task that repairs deterministic timeout diagnostics before another generic timeout fix, so future timeout remediation is driven by concrete failed-step evidence instead of opaque planning timeouts

rules.when: registry pressure is aggregated across multiple project task registries
rules.rule: persist a deterministic `task_registry_pressure_sources` breakdown and use the largest contributor in self-improve reasoning, so pressure follow-ups target the project that dominates the read surface instead of proposing a generic compaction task

rules.when: self-improve sees shared registry pressure but the dominant `task_registry_pressure_sources` entry belongs to another project and the current project's registry stays below the shared threshold
rules.rule: treat the pressure as a blocked cross-project signal and avoid generating a local registry-compaction task, so autonomous work does not burn retries on the wrong project

rules.when: the local task registry stays above 2x the 512KB pressure threshold after an earlier registry-compaction self-improve attempt failed or was shelved
rules.rule: let the `Reduce registry pressure` family bypass only terminal cooldowns and generate one fresh compaction follow-up, while still blocking duplicates when that family is already active

rules.when: dashboard `/api/metrics` reports task-registry pressure
rules.rule: return the same payload-bytes, detected boolean, and primary-surface fields as persisted metrics so live operator reads stay aligned with stored learning signals

rules.when: task-registry pressure is already derived from the shared dashboard snapshot
rules.rule: surface that same pressure object in status and task-registry summaries so operators can see registry-read pressure without opening the metrics view

rules.when: dashboard status or project summaries already expose task-registry pressure
rules.rule: include the dominant `task_registry_pressure_sources` entry and per-project contribution summary there as read-only fields, so operators can identify the registry driving pressure without opening raw metrics or inferring it manually

rules.when: project overview cards already receive per-project task-registry pressure summaries
rules.rule: render the pressure headline, share, and compact source label directly in the card so operators can spot the dominant registry without opening metrics or raw JSON

rules.when: strategy rewrites persisted metrics during a per-project planning pass
rules.rule: recompute metrics from the same multi-project registry set and aggregated on-disk registry sizes used by artifact sync, so one strategy pass cannot weaken shared pressure signals back to a single-registry estimate

rules.when: the task registry backlog grows beyond a single mobile screen
rules.rule: add lightweight filters or collapse completed states before adding more card detail so operators can triage quickly on iPhone-sized layouts

rules.when: queue or orchestrator shell helpers change while the tmux session is already running
rules.rule: restart the queue session before trusting runtime behavior, because long-lived shells keep the helper definitions they sourced at startup

rules.when: tracked queue helper files are changing in a short editing burst
rules.rule: debounce helper-drift reloads until the fingerprint stays stable briefly, so the queue restarts once per burst instead of thrashing through near-identical helper versions

rules.when: tracked strategy-loop helper files are changing in a short editing burst
rules.rule: debounce in-place strategy-loop reloads until the helper fingerprint stays stable briefly, so strategy reruns once per burst instead of restarting on every intermediate save

rules.when: retry counters are written from both shell helpers and embedded Python maintenance paths
rules.rule: use the same hashed retry key everywhere and clear legacy alias files during writes or cleanup so retry state stays deterministic

rules.when: obsolete retry alias files are still present in the runtime retry directory
rules.rule: prune legacy `project__task.retry` aliases during runtime directory setup so observability matches the canonical hashed retry store without waiting for a task rewrite

rules.when: the same orchestrator step keeps failing but the coder message changes between attempts
rules.rule: compare a compact failure fingerprint built from failure category, failed-step text, and reviewer/evaluator outcomes, and stop retrying repeated non-transient failures before a third attempt so retries do not burn budget on the same step

rules.when: automation memory under `$CODEX_HOME` is unset or outside the writable sandbox
rules.rule: mirror the same concise run summary into `projects/<project>/automation-memory/<automation-id>.md` and record that external sync is pending instead of dropping the memory update

rules.when: automation memory under `$CODEX_HOME` is writable again on a later run
rules.rule: merge any mirrored summaries into the real `$CODEX_HOME/automations/<automation-id>/memory.md` path and write the new summary there before falling back to the workspace mirror on an actual path failure

rules.when: a scheduled automation starts with a missing external memory file but a workspace mirror exists
rules.rule: run `scripts/resolve-automation-memory.sh` to resolve the external automation home from `CODEX_HOME` or the default `~/.codex`, hydrate the external memory file from the mirror when possible, and otherwise return the mirror path before picking the next improvement so prior outcomes influence the current run before any new summary is appended

rules.when: self-improve pending tasks are focused on first-pass recovery or approval-backlog drain and the triggering metric has already recovered
rules.rule: auto-shelve those pending proposals once first-pass success returns to at least 50% or active approvals fall back under the backlog threshold, so the bounded active self-improve cap reflects current weaknesses instead of stale recovered work

rules.when: approved work is waiting, the executable queue is empty, and queue starvation is already detected
rules.rule: derive approved-backlog pressure from the stronger of registry state and persisted metrics, then let `Drain approved task backlog` bypass the active self-improve cap during queue starvation so recovery work is not hidden by stale or sparse registry snapshots

rules.when: planner, coder, or orchestrator builds project memory for a project that declares an `automation_id`
rules.rule: append a short recent automation-memory section via the shared resolver so agent context inherits recent scheduled-run outcomes mechanically instead of depending on prompt-only memory instructions

rules.when: an external scheduled runner needs automation memory before choosing the next improvement
rules.rule: call `scripts/prepare-automation-context.sh <project> <recent-lines>` and consume its JSON payload so memory resolution, recent entries, and project file paths come from one deterministic wrapper instead of prompt-only shell steps

rules.when: self-improve has multiple viable follow-up candidates and recent automation memory records a successful `next=` recommendation
rules.rule: move that matching title to the front of the filtered self-improve submission list before applying submission limits, so scheduled runs continue the last verified next step without overriding stronger live gating signals

rules.when: strategy-loop reads persisted success_rate to decide whether a small approved backlog should block new generation
rules.rule: only treat low success_rate as a gating health signal when metrics include real execution records (`total_tasks > 0`), so zero-record snapshots do not freeze strategy on fallback `0` values

rules.when: automation run summaries are persisted successfully to the external `$CODEX_HOME` memory path
rules.rule: append the same summary to the workspace automation mirror as well, so fallback memory stays current and a later external-path loss can still recover the latest learned outcomes

rules.when: creating or loading metadata for a managed project outside codex-agent-system
rules.rule: require an explicit external workspace path before execution; do not default runtime work into projects/<name> inside Codex Control

rules.when: codex exec hits a persistent authentication failure
rules.rule: cache the auth failure reason briefly, pause queue processing while auth is unavailable, and skip repeated live codex calls until the cooldown expires

rules.when: a cached Codex auth failure is blocking the queue
rules.rule: surface the blocker reason and remaining cooldown directly in dashboard status and next-action messaging before inviting retries or new approvals

rules.when: Codex auth is blocked while operators review pending approvals
rules.rule: reject dashboard approval transitions immediately, but keep pending task edits available so operators can prepare work before auth recovers

rules.when: a queue worker timeout can race with run-context success persistence
rules.rule: reuse the existing late-success detector with a short bounded grace window before recording timeout failure, so persisted success evidence wins without adding unbounded waits

rules.when: a run has already persisted terminal execution evidence before the lane wrapper times out
rules.rule: treat persisted `execution_context.result` as the source of truth and downgrade the timeout to the recorded success or failure outcome instead of appending a new timeout classification

rules.when: persisted timeout pressure is derived from timeout task-log records that carry an exact registry task id
rules.rule: ignore timeout records whose linked registry task has already persisted success, so strategy reacts to unresolved timeout pressure instead of stale reconciled failures

rules.when: dashboard `/api/metrics` summarizes timeout pressure from task-log records
rules.rule: apply the same unresolved-timeout reconciliation used by persisted metrics and project health, so live operator metrics do not overcount already-recovered timeout failures

rules.when: pending approval task text or project metadata needs correction from mobile
rules.rule: edit the task inline in the dashboard before queue handoff and append an audit history entry for the change

rules.when: the dashboard offers a direct queue action outside the approval backlog
rules.rule: remove or downgrade the action into pending approval until deterministic server-side task shaping exists; do not let vague raw prompts or compatibility endpoints bypass human review

rules.when: strategy-seeded or anomaly-generated tasks have already failed twice with the same intent
rules.rule: treat the failed equivalents as saturated and stop recreating the same title/template until a different bounded experiment is available

rules.when: strategy, queue guards, and metrics all reason about repeated failed equivalents
rules.rule: keep the saturation threshold aligned at two failed equivalents across code paths so the loop stops recreating the same experiment as soon as shared learning marks it saturated

rules.when: bounded child retries under the same failed root have already failed twice
rules.rule: stop generating another `bounded_failed_step_child` descendant for that root and fall back to a different strategy family instead of burning more retries on the same decomposition path

rules.when: distinct task-registry records share the same queue text
rules.rule: scope retry state to the selected registry task id and fall back to execution.attempt instead of reusing title-keyed retry files across different task instances

rules.when: a queue lane claims one registry task among several same-title siblings
rules.rule: carry the claimed task id through execution-state syncs so start/completion/failure updates mutate the exact claimed record instead of re-resolving by queue text

rules.when: post-run execution context is persisted after a same-title task was claimed explicitly
rules.rule: thread the claimed task id into run-context persistence as well, so failure_context and execution_context attach to the exact claimed record instead of the most recently updated same-title sibling

rules.when: a same-title lease needs to be released after an explicit claim
rules.rule: release the lease by claimed task id when available, instead of freeing whichever same-title approved/running record happens to match first

rules.when: the strategy loop intentionally stops retrying a repeated failed system task
rules.rule: surface the saturation state in task-registry summaries so operators know to pick a different bounded experiment instead of assuming the loop is stuck

rules.when: strategy saturation is only visible in dashboard task summaries
rules.rule: persist a compact saturation count and boolean in metrics.json so later decision paths can reuse repeated-failure signals without rescanning the full registry

rules.when: auto approval is enabled for strategy seed or anomaly work and an equivalent strategy family has already failed
rules.rule: keep the next strategy task in pending_approval instead of auto-queuing it so observed failures influence the next attempt before retry budget is spent again

rules.when: strategy is blocked behind pending approval tasks and creates no new board updates
rules.rule: report the blocker explicitly in strategy output, and mention saturation recovery when that pending task is the only remaining board item, so the next operator decision is guided instead of hidden behind a generic no-op

rules.when: older failed tasks are missing `failed_step` but still keep deterministic task intent, title, or task-log evidence
rules.rule: backfill `execution_context.failed_step` and `failure_context.failed_step` during strategy maintenance before follow-up selection, so historical failures still influence bounded-child generation and failed-task prioritization

rules.when: the only pending approval is a strategy saturation-recovery task
rules.rule: persist the saturated task id/title/template as structured metadata and reuse it in approval messaging so operators choose a genuinely different bounded experiment instead of re-approving the same failed family

rules.when: strategy is blocked on a legacy saturation-recovery pending approval before any dashboard read repairs it
rules.rule: backfill the same saturation metadata, rerouted provider, and compact replacement title during the strategy pass itself so scheduled runs report the learned blocker deterministically from tasks.json

rules.when: a saturation-recovery task replaces a saturated bounded child follow-up that already recorded the failed step
rules.rule: derive the pending approval title from the failed step's narrowest surviving constraint before falling back to a generic replacement title, so approval carries one concrete bounded experiment instead of another meta retry

rules.when: strategy creates a new saturation-recovery pending approval from the latest saturated failure
rules.rule: apply the same derived title, context hint, and alternate-provider reroute at creation time instead of relying on a later repair pass, so scheduled runs surface one concrete approval immediately

rules.when: strategy auto-repairs a saturation-recovery pending approval that already carries the correct rerouted provider
rules.rule: preserve the existing provider-selection timestamp and skip the write entirely unless the provider choice or reroute reason changed, so repeated strategy passes stop appending duplicate repair history

rules.when: a saturation-recovery pending approval already carries dashboard-normalized task_intent arrays
rules.rule: normalize the strategy repair intent to preserve empty constraints, success_signals, and affected_files lists so semantically unchanged approvals do not churn updated_at or append duplicate auto_repair history

rules.when: pending approval tasks are the only remaining backlog
rules.rule: persist a compact `pending_approval_blocked_detected` signal through shared metrics and dashboard guard paths so later decisions can reuse the operator-held blocker without misclassifying it as queue starvation

rules.when: strategy is already blocked on pending approvals with no executable work left
rules.rule: do not create additional pending follow-ups, external review tasks, or enterprise seeds until the operator clears the existing backlog, so strategy does not deepen its own approval blocker

rules.when: pending approvals are the only remaining actionable backlog
rules.rule: surface one deterministic approval recommendation, preferring the oldest pending review, so operators clear the blocker in a stable order instead of choosing arbitrarily

rules.when: enterprise readiness seeding has multiple viable templates and some have already failed more often than others
rules.rule: prefer the least-failed template first so task selection reuses failure history instead of re-seeding the same weaker experiment

rules.when: enterprise readiness seed templates are tied on failed-equivalent count
rules.rule: prefer categories with a positive observed win rate in the current project before falling back to static template order, so future enterprise seeds reuse recent outcomes instead of creation order

rules.when: multiple failed-task follow-ups are competing for a limited pending-approval slot
rules.rule: prefer source families from categories with a positive observed project-local win rate before falling back to pure recency, so bounded follow-ups learn from the categories that have already resolved successfully

rules.when: strategy category ranking has no resolved project-local history for a category
rules.rule: fall back to the configured category success prior from priority.json, but keep any positive local observed win rate ahead of that prior so early planning stays deterministic without overriding real project evidence

rules.when: persistent loop effort is already detected and enterprise seed templates are tied on saturation plus evidence source
rules.rule: prefer the category with lower observed loop effort before comparing raw success-rate strength, so enterprise seeding spends the next slot reducing execution drag instead of repeating the heavier category

rules.when: provider histories for a category are tied on learned success rate and task count
rules.rule: prefer the provider with the lower avg total step attempts, so routing reuses the same bounded retry cap while still learning which provider finishes with less aggregate loop effort

rules.when: provider routing rules are regenerated from learned provider stats
rules.rule: refresh provider-routing.json alongside provider-stats.json and break equal success/task-count ties with lower avg total step attempts so persisted routing stays aligned with learned lower-effort choices

rules.when: retry churn or queue starvation is derived from persisted task state
rules.rule: persist the compact board-health booleans through the shared task-metrics path so strategy, sync, and dashboard reuse the same deterministic signal

rules.when: board-health metrics classify queue starvation while tasks are only waiting in pending approval
rules.rule: treat pending approval as operator-held backlog instead of executable starvation, and only flag queue starvation when approved or running work exists without active execution progress

rules.when: persisted metrics are refreshed in a multi-project workspace with dedicated external task registries
rules.rule: aggregate every known project task_registry_file through the shared artifact-sync path instead of only `codex-memory/tasks.json`, so approved backlog, board-health signals, and learning stay aligned with the dashboard's cross-project view

rules.when: strategy consumes persisted retry-churn health to seed follow-up work
rules.rule: treat the shared retry-churn signal as actionable only when current approved, running, or stale-running work still carries retry pressure; do not seed from historical multi-attempt resolutions alone

rules.when: stale running tasks are reconciled before strategy plans new anomaly work
rules.rule: remove the separate runtime-state mismatch anomaly and let queue-drain or retry-pressure decisions operate on the reconciled registry state instead of duplicating the stale-running diagnosis

rules.when: external web research is used to influence self-improvement
rules.rule: ingest only bounded configured feeds into a deterministic snapshot and route each fresh external signal through pending approval before broader system changes are derived

rules.when: strategy performs external web or media research autonomously
rules.rule: run the research worker inside Docker, keep the source list explicitly configured, and prefer transcript- or subtitle-backed media inputs so the resulting knowledge snapshot stays deterministic and reviewable

rules.when: queue-side low-completion anomaly seeding considers the `queue_drain_completion_guard` buffer task after two equivalent failed runs
rules.rule: treat that buffer experiment as saturated and do not auto-approve another copy until a different bounded follow-up is available

rules.when: strategy planning sees the `system_work_buffer` queue-drain family already fail twice
rules.rule: skip that saturated buffer template and let the next bounded backlog fallback seed instead of recreating the same pending-approval task

rules.when: queue-drain buffer seeding just saw an equivalent `queue_drain_completion_guard` or `system_work_buffer` task complete or get rejected recently
rules.rule: treat the recent resolved attempt as a short cooldown and suppress immediate reseeding on both the strategy and queue-side paths until the cooldown expires, so the system learns to pause before recreating the same buffer task

rules.when: browser-based dashboard acceptance is used to validate a redesign
rules.rule: assert rendered hierarchy and operator interactions in a live browser session instead of trusting screenshot artifacts alone; verify search and density controls directly in the page

rules.when: bounded external research can influence future planning
rules.rule: persist compact research freshness, error, and latest-source provenance in shared metrics so operators and later decision paths can see whether external signals are current before acting on them

rules.when: strategy seeds a follow-up from an external research signal
rules.rule: reuse the persisted research status/error snapshot to lower task confidence when shared external-signal metrics are stale or erroring, so external follow-ups do not outrank stronger internal evidence

rules.when: dashboard search/highlight behavior watches the board for refresh mutations
rules.rule: never observe subtree mutations while also rewriting descendant innerHTML for highlights; watch only structural list changes or guard the observer so board tooling cannot trigger an unresponsive browser loop

rules.when: pending approval tasks are auto-repaired into approval-ready titles and shapes
rules.rule: preserve strategy-specific context in the repaired title and ignore timestamp-only task_shape diffs so repeated dashboard reads do not rewrite the same task again

rules.when: the only pending approval is a strategy saturation-recovery task
rules.rule: auto-repair the generic recovery title into a concrete replacement objective using the stored saturated-task metadata before approval, so queue handoff reuses failure history instead of enqueuing a vague meta task

rules.when: a strategy saturation-recovery task already identifies the saturated experiment it replaces
rules.rule: carry the saturated experiment's recorded provider into the repaired replacement task as an explicit reroute to the alternate provider, so approval preserves the most relevant execution-learning signal instead of defaulting back to the provider that already saturated

rules.when: enterprise-readiness strategy seeds a new pending approval task
rules.rule: persist the same compact task_intent metadata used by other strategy paths so approval shaping, metrics, and later strategy decisions can reuse the seed deterministically

rules.when: bounded failed-step follow-up tasks inherit long file-scoped step text from a failed plan
rules.rule: auto-repair them into compact approval-ready objective titles keyed to the failed strategy signal, so the approval queue does not stall on deterministic child tasks

rules.when: pending approval still contains board-health follow-ups sourced from persisted retry-churn or first-pass strategy families
rules.rule: compact them to the family-level approval title before rendering or persisting the board row, so approval readiness and duplicate detection stay deterministic

rules.when: the resident dashboard backend entrypoint changes after agentctl started the session
rules.rule: treat `codex-dashboard/server.js` drift the same as shell-helper drift and require a reload before trusting approval reshaping or prompt-intake behavior

rules.when: runtime reload drift is marked restart-needed while pending approvals are still open
rules.rule: block approval handoff server-side and surface the restart reason directly in the approval UI so stale dashboard logic cannot enqueue new work

rules.when: a recurring queue-buffer seed family has a newer completed equivalent after older failures
rules.rule: count only failures since the latest success and let the queue-drain buffer recur when backlog pressure returns, instead of keeping the family permanently saturated from stale failures

rules.when: approval handoff is blocked by runtime reload drift
rules.rule: show the exact existing `agentctl.sh reload` workflow in the approval surface so operators can recover without leaving the pending queue guessing at the next step

rules.when: runtime helper fingerprints are computed inside minimal fixtures or partial worktrees
rules.rule: hash missing tracked helper files as a deterministic sentinel instead of failing, so reload-drift detection still works when optional runtime surfaces like the dashboard are absent

rules.when: orchestrator runs span multiple plan steps with per-step retries
rules.rule: persist the bounded max retry count as `attempts` and track aggregate loop effort separately as `total_step_attempts`, so safety limits, provider learning, and failure context do not treat normal multi-step work as excess retries

rules.when: dashboard task details summarize execution attempts after bounded retry accounting is introduced
rules.rule: show aggregate loop effort as `total_step_attempts` only when it exceeds the bounded retry count, so operators can see real multi-step work without mistaking it for a retry-budget violation

rules.when: persisted metrics summarize task pressure after bounded retry accounting is introduced
rules.rule: track loop effort from `total_step_attempts - attempts` at the task level instead of treating bounded retry counts as a proxy for multi-step work, so future analysis can separate retry pressure from normal execution depth

rules.when: persistent loop effort is already detected and multiple failed follow-up families are competing
rules.rule: keep existing learned success signals first, but break the remaining tie toward the lower-effort bounded follow-up before recency so strategy spends the next slot reducing execution drag instead of retrying broader work

rules.when: persistent loop effort is already detected and enterprise seed templates are tied on failed-equivalent and category-success ranking
rules.rule: prefer categories with lower observed extra step attempts before static template order so enterprise backlog growth shifts toward work that has executed with less drag

rules.when: an approved task was marked `already_queued` at approval time but its live queue entry later disappears
rules.rule: treat `already_queued` as a recoverable queue handoff state and enqueue the approved task again when it is no longer present in the queue or running set, so duplicate-safe approval does not strand approved work until a runtime restart

rules.when: strategy mutates the task board and then persists `codex-learning/metrics.json`
rules.rule: recompute metrics with the shared persisted-metrics builder and the current external-signal snapshot, so retry pressure, saturation, and research freshness stay aligned with the post-strategy state

rules.when: the current strategy run has sparse task-log records but persisted board-health metrics still show queue starvation or active retry pressure
rules.rule: reuse the persisted board-health snapshot to seed the existing system-work buffer guard when the current backlog still carries matching starvation or retry-pressure signals, so prior outcomes still influence task selection before fresh logs accumulate again

rules.when: all enterprise strategy seed families are saturated and the board has no actionable tasks
rules.rule: create one bounded pending-approval saturation-recovery task instead of returning a silent strategy no-op, so operators can choose a different experiment without repeating the saturated templates

rules.when: a strategy pass makes no new board mutations but pending or approved backlog still exists
rules.rule: persist the existing approval backlog into `strategy-latest.json` and keep fresh mutations in a separate `board_updates` list, so operators and loop health can see the real board state without misreporting every pass as a new update

rules.when: priority learning is regenerated from task-registry outcomes and later reused by strategy
rules.rule: treat `completed` tasks as successful outcomes when computing `observed_success_rate`, and preserve that field when strategy reads `priority.json`, so learned category priors actually influence later seed ranking

rules.when: shared metrics show the task-registry payload is already under pressure
rules.rule: persist a compact payload-bytes signal and prefer one bounded performance seed ahead of other enterprise templates, so strategy reacts to registry scale before repeated full-read paths become the next bottleneck

rules.when: task-registry payload pressure is detected before finer read telemetry exists
rules.rule: target the dashboard read path first and keep that surface in the seeded task metadata, because the fixed dashboard poll remains the highest-frequency registry reader and later saturation should apply to that narrower experiment instead of a generic performance title

rules.when: persisted metrics show repeated queue timeouts across multiple runs
rules.rule: prioritize one bounded timeout-reduction experiment ahead of generic enterprise backlog work so failure history changes the next stability decision before more retry budget is burned

rules.when: strategy reseeds a timeout-reduction enterprise task after earlier timeout-focused work already captured concrete scope
rules.rule: reuse the richest prior timeout task_intent context, constraints, success signals, and observed example metadata instead of creating a blank generic timeout approval, so future timeout work stays bounded by what the system already learned

rules.when: dashboard repair or approval touches a pending `enterprise_timeout_stability` task that still carries generic timeout guidance
rules.rule: hydrate its task_intent and observed timeout example fields from the richest prior timeout-focused task before queue handoff, so approval_execution_brief, execution_brief, and queue_handoff preserve the bounded timeout scope already learned

rules.when: dashboard read paths repeatedly derive project task-registry targets or policy gates from stable `project.json` and `policy.json` files
rules.rule: cache those small project config reads behind file-signature checks so multi-project polling stops rereading unchanged config while still invalidating deterministically on edits

rules.when: a legacy strategy saturation-recovery task predates structured metadata but still names the saturated failure in its reason text
rules.rule: backfill the missing saturation metadata from the matched failed task during pending-approval repair, so the dashboard can reshape and approve the replacement experiment deterministically

rules.when: a saturation-recovery approval is derived from a failed bounded child that already recorded one deterministic verification command
rules.rule: carry that exact verification command into the repaired approval shape instead of leaving verification blank, so the next approval preserves both the bounded fix target and its pass/fail check

rules.when: strategy is blocked by one pending approval task that already persists a deterministic verification command
rules.rule: surface that verification command in the strategy summary and board snapshot so operators can approve from the top-level dashboard without reopening the task details

rules.when: dashboard repair or edit paths rebuild a pending task shape around a saturation-recovery approval
rules.rule: preserve any existing deterministic verification_command unless a new non-empty command is derived, so read-time normalization does not erase approval guidance and trigger repeated strategy auto-repairs

rules.when: a queue lane times out after the orchestrator already appended a terminal `tasks.log` record but before registry run-context persistence finishes
rules.rule: reuse the latest matching task-log SUCCESS or FAILURE record written after the active lease timestamp during timeout reconciliation so late bookkeeping is not misclassified as a fresh timeout

rules.when: claimed queue tasks can persist terminal evidence a few seconds after the lane wrapper times out
rules.rule: keep the late-timeout reconciliation window short but wide enough to poll roughly four seconds past the timeout boundary, so exact task-id evidence can win before a fresh timeout failure is recorded

rules.when: persisted timeout pressure still includes legacy timeout task-log records that predate stored task ids
rules.rule: ignore a legacy timeout record once a later SUCCESS task-log entry exists for the same project and normalized task title, so pre-task-id evidence stops inflating current timeout pressure after the work eventually succeeds

rules.when: planner is asked to retry the exact same project task title after an unresolved zero-step timeout already consumed the full planning budget
rules.rule: skip the live planner provider call and reuse the deterministic fallback planner path immediately, so repeated attempts spend time on bounded implementation guidance instead of burning another planning-only timeout

rules.when: planner agent execution falls back after a similar task already failed with bounded guidance
rules.rule: reuse the matched task's persisted failed_step and verification_command in the fallback plan so retries stay concrete instead of collapsing back to generic implementation steps

rules.when: planner agent execution falls back for a task that already carries structured task_intent metadata but no persisted failed_step yet
rules.rule: derive the implementation step from the task_intent objective, affected files, context hint, and constraints so fallback plans stay bounded and deterministic instead of defaulting to a generic implementation placeholder

rules.when: a successful planner response still contains the generic implementation or lightweight-verification placeholder after related task history already narrowed the work
rules.rule: repair the plan before execution by preferring the strongest non-generic failed_step from similar tasks and the best explicit verification_command, so prior failures influence the next attempt even when the planner provider returned a vague but schema-valid plan

rules.when: coder fallback receives the generic implementation placeholder but task_intent or prior failure context already narrows the work
rules.rule: score similar tasks the same way as planner repair, prefer the strongest non-generic failed_step, and reuse the best explicit verification_command in the fallback response so the next retry inherits the richest bounded guidance instead of the first generic match

rules.when: reviewer or evaluator falls back after coder already recovered a bounded retry step for a generic implementation placeholder
rules.rule: echo the same bounded step and preferred verification command in retry findings and evaluation reasons so downstream retries preserve the narrowed work instead of regressing to generic failure messaging

rules.when: coder retries a generic implementation step after a same-run reviewer or evaluator already returned bounded retry guidance
rules.rule: prefer the latest bounded retry step and preferred verification command from the prior-attempt feedback payload before scanning older similar-task history, so same-run evidence wins over weaker historical matches

rules.when: strategy plans follow-up work for a non-root project that configures its own task registry file
rules.rule: read and write board updates through that project's configured task_registry_file, but keep shared metrics aggregation rooted in the primary registry discovery path so per-project planning and cross-project learning stay aligned

rules.when: planner or coder executes an approved task that already has a current task registry record with execution_brief, task_intent, or task_shape metadata
rules.rule: prefer the exact current task by task_id over fuzzy similar-task matches, and reuse its stored verification_command before broader keyword heuristics so approved handoff guidance survives into execution retries

rules.when: persisting failed-task run context into the task registry
rules.rule: keep `failure_context` limited to the compact follow-up fields strategy needs, and leave richer terminal metrics on `execution_context` so lifecycle writes stay deterministic and backward-compatible

rules.when: task-registry pressure is already present in top-level task summaries
rules.rule: surface a warning cue directly in the task summary card with payload size and read surface so mobile operators can spot registry-read pressure without opening the metrics panel

rules.when: saturation recovery has already failed for one experiment family but the latest saturated weakness belongs to a different family
rules.rule: count failed `strategy_saturation_rescue` attempts per replaced target, not globally across every rescue task, so one stale rescue family cannot block a fresh bounded recovery for the current saturated weakness

rules.when: dashboard auto-approve or approval spotlight actions operate on tasks aggregated from multiple projects
rules.rule: carry the task project alongside the task id through client controls and server auto-approve helpers, so duplicate ids across projects cannot block or mutate the wrong record

rules.when: dashboard dependency summaries or timeout reconciliation look up task ids across aggregated project registries
rules.rule: key lookup helpers by `(project,id)` first and only fall back to bare ids when they are globally unique, so duplicate ids across projects cannot block the wrong dependency or keep stale timeout pressure alive

rules.when: orchestrator failures are written into `codex-memory/tasks.log` for later metrics or repeated-failure analysis
rules.rule: copy the same compact failed-step context and deterministic failure kind used by the task registry into the task-log record, so later learning can group step failures instead of leaving most failures as `unknown`

rules.when: a strategy saturation-recovery task points at another saturation-recovery task instead of the original saturated experiment
rules.rule: flatten the recovery target back to the underlying failed experiment during repair and threshold checks, so strategy stops creating nested `Replace Replace ...` approvals and counts rescue failures against the real saturated family

rules.when: a failed task already comes from `strategy::saturation-recovery`
rules.rule: do not spawn an ordinary `bounded_failed_step_child` from that rescue failure; skip straight to the rescue-family replacement logic so strategy keeps proposing a new bounded experiment for the saturated weakness instead of degrading into verification-only child churn

rules.when: a saturated anomaly root already has a newer bounded failed descendant in the same root family
rules.rule: keep the rescue metadata pointed at the saturated root for thresholding, but shape the replacement title and context from the most concrete failed descendant so the next approval does not just restate the original broad anomaly

rules.when: a completed `strategy_saturation_rescue` only verifies, checks, or documents a saturated replacement
rules.rule: do not treat that completion as resolution of the underlying saturated target when deciding whether another rescue is needed, because bounded validation evidence alone should not suppress the next real replacement experiment

rules.when: a broad failed step starts with `Inspect ...` but then already names a concrete patch/edit/write action
rules.rule: derive the bounded child from that concrete action clause instead of repeating the full inspect prefix, so follow-up tasks stay implementation-focused and do not burn another run re-documenting context that was already part of the failed step

rules.when: a broad failed step is inspection-only and does not yet name a concrete patch/edit/write action
rules.rule: generate a bounded inventory/documentation follow-up instead of a normal implementation child, so the next run records the missing state explicitly before another code-change retry is queued

rules.when: the newest saturated experiment has already exhausted its rescue budget but older saturated families are still unresolved
rules.rule: scan saturated failures by recency and pick the first target whose rescue family still has budget and no actionable equivalent, so one over-saturated rescue target does not stall the whole board

rules.when: strategy has limited backlog slots and some failed roots still have no persisted failed_step or bounded child context
rules.rule: rank failed roots with concrete failed-step context ahead of no-context failures, so scarce follow-up slots go first to executable retries instead of another generic context-recovery loop

rules.when: a `bounded_learning_inventory` follow-up reaches planner or coder fallback guidance
rules.rule: preserve the task's inspect-and-write inventory experiment plus a file-existence verification command, instead of degrading it into a generic implementation step that invites another failed pseudo-code run

rules.when: an inspect-only failed step already names exact source files before generating or revisiting a `bounded_learning_inventory` follow-up
rules.rule: carry those file hints into the follow-up task_intent and auto-repair pending inventory tasks from the parent failure context, so later runs can target the right files without re-reading the broader failed step

rules.when: a root goal has accumulated 3+ failed tasks under different task IDs
rules.rule: shelve the root goal instead of seeding another follow-up experiment to prevent unbounded retry cascading

rules.when: the coder agent fails with exit code 1 on multi-file edit tasks
rules.rule: prefer simpler single-file tasks that match the coder demonstrated capability envelope

rules.when: the overall failure rate exceeds 70%
rules.rule: reduce task complexity and increase task specificity before generating new work

rules.when: codex CLI is called from lib.sh run_codex_exec
rules.rule: validate that the -a (ask-for-approval) flag uses a valid value from the set {untrusted, on-failure, on-request, never}; invalid values like auto cause immediate silent failure of all provider calls

rules.when: the learner agent analyzes task failures
rules.rule: include actual error messages from .codex.log and .claude.log files in the analysis prompt so the learner can identify systemic issues like CLI flag errors or auth failures, not just abstract failure counts

rules.when: self-improve.sh runs its analysis cycle
rules.rule: check provider CLI health (flag validity, CLI availability, auth state) before generating improvement tasks, so configuration drift is detected early instead of after dozens of failed tasks

rules.when: system success rate is below 30%
rules.rule: prefer inventory and detection tasks over implementation tasks; inventory tasks succeed at ~50% while multi-file implementation tasks succeed at <10%

rules.when: creating a new task from a failed root goal
rules.rule: check if an equivalent task (same title prefix) already exists as failed in the registry; if so, require a materially different approach or decompose into read-only inventory first

rules.when: a root goal has accumulated 3+ failures across templates
rules.rule: decompose into inventory-first workflow: generate a read-only inventory task, then derive implementation tasks only from verified inventory findings

rules.when: self-improve.sh validates Codex CLI health
rules.rule: read the approval mode from a shared lib.sh helper instead of grepping source text, so unrelated example strings cannot trigger false invalid-flag errors

rules.when: self-improve.sh sees a large approved or pending backlog while success remains low or registry pressure is already detected
rules.rule: suppress new self-improvement experiments and keep at most one backlog-drain follow-up, so autonomous task generation does not deepen board saturation faster than execution can recover

rules.when: strategy-loop decides whether low success should pause new planning work
rules.rule: count live approved tasks from the project task registry before falling back to persisted metrics, and only keep the low-success gate active when executable backlog pressure or shared saturation signals still exist, so drained boards can resume strategy work instead of staying frozen on stale or unconditional metrics

rules.when: orchestrator retries a failed step and builds an inline Python retry-context helper
rules.rule: keep the helper syntactically valid and cover the retry branch with a regression test, so retry enrichment adds prior failure context instead of crashing with a heredoc parse error

rules.when: orchestrator failure-classification logic runs in the main retry loop rather than inside a shell function
rules.rule: do not use bash `local` declarations in that path and keep a deterministic retry-branch regression test, so reviewer/evaluator rejections cannot crash the run before bounded retries execute

rules.when: self-improve.sh deduplicates stable improvement title families
rules.rule: block families that already have active work or a recent terminal attempt inside a bounded cooldown, use a 24h cooldown for failed `self-improve` families even after one terminal failure, and only let stale terminal families resurface after that window so the loop does not retry the same autonomous fix before new evidence exists

rules.when: a project already has three or more active self-improve tasks in pending_approval, approved, queued, or running
rules.rule: suppress new non-emergency self-improve submissions until that backlog drains, and only bypass the cap for zero-step-timeout or extreme local registry-pressure emergencies so autonomous follow-ups deepen focus instead of queue spread

rules.when: queue workers and self-improve tasks rely on the shared default retry budget
rules.rule: keep the default `MAX_AGENT_RETRIES` aligned to the documented policy value of 2, so newly generated tasks, retry telemetry, and live queue behavior share the same deterministic cap

rules.when: self-improve.sh completes an analysis cycle for dashboard or automation consumers
rules.rule: write one atomic `codex-learning/self-improve-run.json` artifact with generated/submitted/skipped counts plus the dominant gating reason, so downstream readers can consume the latest decision outcome without scraping free-form logs

rules.when: self-improve overload gating is active because backlog, registry pressure, or weak success rate coincide with execution failures
rules.rule: prioritize one root-cause stabilization task such as timeout reduction or retry-churn repair ahead of a generic backlog-drain task, so autonomous follow-up addresses the failure driver instead of only its queue symptom

rules.when: self-improve overload gating must choose between multiple root-cause stabilization families
rules.rule: rank the candidates by current signal severity and recent title-family outcomes, and penalize families that already failed recently without a newer success before falling back to static template order, so overload follow-up work shifts toward the best-supported unresolved weakness

rules.when: a structured self-improve run artifact is already available on disk
rules.rule: surface its normalized status, counts, and dominant gating reason in dashboard metrics, so operators can see the latest autonomous decision without opening logs or parsing JSON manually

rules.when: self-improve overload gating filters multiple candidate families down to one preserved task
rules.rule: persist the preserved family plus compact candidate scores and blocked-family reasons in the run artifact and normalized dashboard summary, so later operators and automations can audit why one overload fix was chosen without reconstructing the ranking from logs

rules.when: operators inspect project-scoped dashboard summaries
rules.rule: thread the self-improve run artifact into project summaries only for the matching project and return a deterministic unavailable payload for others, so narrowed workflows keep the latest autonomous decision visible without leaking cross-project state

rules.when: self-improve prioritizes retry-classification repair because coverage is low
rules.rule: surface the classified and total retry counts in the normalized dashboard self-improve summary, so operators can see why deterministic failure-capture repair outranks broader retry tuning

rules.when: project overview cards already summarize registry pressure and self-improve exposes an active operator signal
rules.rule: promote the normalized self-improve operator signal into the project overview card before generic pressure callouts, so cross-project triage keeps the current autonomous focus visible without opening detailed metrics

rules.when: self-improve overload gating preserves one candidate from several ranked families
rules.rule: persist the sorted overload candidates with explicit rank and selected status in `codex-learning/self-improve-run.json`, so automation and dashboard consumers can audit why one family won without reconstructing the ranking from logs

rules.when: retry analysis rows keep stable `project` plus `task_id` but historical entries still lack `error_text`
rules.rule: fallback to the nearest persisted `failure_kind` in `codex-memory/tasks.log` when computing retry-classification coverage, so self-improve can use existing failure evidence immediately instead of waiting for new enriched retry events

rules.when: self-improve sees missing `approved_tasks`, `pending_approval_tasks`, or similar core metrics in `metrics.json`
rules.rule: refresh persisted metrics from `tasks.json` and `tasks.log` before ranking improvements, but preserve complete shared snapshots instead of overwriting them with narrower local data

rules.when: self-improve repairs or skips incomplete metrics before analysis
rules.rule: persist the metrics-input status, reason, and missing-key set in `codex-learning/self-improve-run.json` and the normalized dashboard summary, so later runs and operators can see whether the decision used complete inputs or a repaired snapshot

rules.when: self-improve sees a complete `metrics.json` that is older than non-empty task, task-log, or meaningful external-signal artifacts
rules.rule: refresh persisted metrics before ranking improvements, but ignore empty placeholder `tasks.log` or external-signal snapshots so freshness repair follows real evidence instead of startup side effects

rules.when: self-improve sees complete persisted metrics with bounded rate fields outside the valid 0..1 range
rules.rule: treat the snapshot as invalid decision input and refresh metrics from live task artifacts before ranking improvements, so stale or corrupt persisted rates cannot bias autonomous task selection

rules.when: self-improve run artifacts already persist metrics-input repair status but no stronger retry-coverage or overload signal is active
rules.rule: promote stale-or-repaired metrics-input state into the normalized self-improve operator signal so dashboard overview cards expose decision-input quality without opening the raw run artifact

rules.when: scheduled automation startup runs through `scripts/prepare-automation-context.sh` and the persisted metrics snapshot is missing, stale, or contains bounded rates outside 0..1
rules.rule: refresh `codex-learning/metrics.json` from live task artifacts before emitting automation context so scheduled runs and operators do not inherit stale decision inputs from an older metrics snapshot

rules.when: zero-step timeout emergency is active and prior timeout-family outcomes already cooled down or exhausted the generic timeout remediation
rules.rule: generate the narrower `Cap pre-step planning budget` self-improve task alongside the generic timeout fix so past timeout failures steer the next remediation toward the learned 60s planning cap instead of repeating another broad timeout experiment

rules.when: dashboard project overview cards surface a self-improve operator signal while active self-improve tasks are already pending, approved, queued, or running
rules.rule: show the active self-improve backlog count and cap directly in the overview detail so operators can see why autonomous improvement is blocked without opening raw run artifacts

rules.when: strategy sees a `pending_approval` or `approved` task whose title already failed 5+ times in `tasks.log`
rules.rule: auto-shelve the active zombie backlog entry with `zombie_guard` history before backlog gating, and never recreate the same title in the same strategy pass

rules.when: self-improve cooldown evaluates whether emergency recovery work should stay suppressed
rules.rule: recompute project-local stale-pipeline and zero-step-timeout signals from `tasks.json` and `tasks.log` before keeping cooldown active, because persisted metrics can lag the live execution evidence

rules.when: validate-metrics.sh runs in sandbox with fewer registries
rules.rule: skip cross-project field corrections to prevent overcorrection of shared metrics

rules.when: review_rejection dominates retry failures at 44%
rules.rule: diff coder output against reviewer objection and inject targeted fix hint into retry prompt

rules.when: timeout dominates at 29% of retries
rules.rule: cap planning to 60s before first step execution and abort steps exceeding 80% of timeout budget

rules.when: learner overwrites rules each run
rules.rule: accumulate rules with dedup at 65% similarity threshold and cap at 20

rules.when: zero-step timeouts consume 90% of timeout failures
rules.rule: orchestrator must begin first step execution within 60s of run start

rules.when: evaluator scores SUCCESS tasks as 0
rules.rule: post-LLM validation clamp enforcing score >= 5 when status=success

rules.when: task family succeeds 3+ times for same weakness
rules.rule: cap at GLOBAL_FAMILY_SUCCESS_CAP=3 to prevent duplicated work

rules.when: zombie tasks fail 5+ times across all attempts
rules.rule: shelve permanently via zombie guard — do not requeue or re-approve

rules.when: shell scripts are submitted by coder
rules.rule: must pass bash -n syntax check before marking step complete

rules.when: python scripts are submitted by coder
rules.rule: must pass ast.parse validation before marking step complete

rules.when: sandbox_restriction or missing_environment causes failure
rules.rule: mark as environment-blocked rather than retrying — prevents infinite retry loops

rules.when: task exists in queue file but not registry
rules.rule: verify bidirectional consistency before dispatch to prevent orphan execution

rules.when: memory files grow beyond 7 days of entries
rules.rule: prune and archive entries older than 7 days to *-archive files

rules.when: metrics.json is refreshed
rules.rule: recompute from registry every sync — stale metrics cause cascading false signals

rules.when: task touches more than 3 files per step
rules.rule: split into subtasks — file-count correlates with timeout and step_not_completed

rules.when: step_not_completed is dominant retry category
rules.rule: ensure coder outputs include explicit completion markers the reviewer can verify

rules.when: template values appear in LLM prompts
rules.rule: use descriptive markers like <CALCULATE THIS> instead of literal defaults that get copied verbatim

rules.when: trivial changes (comments, tests, single-line fixes) are rejected
rules.rule: calibrate reviewer leniency — scope-aware threshold reduces unnecessary re-work on low-risk changes

rules.when: topic files exceed 50-line rolling window cap
rules.rule: prune to keep only most recent 50 entries per topic

rules.when: pipeline idle with recent_success_rate > 0.90
rules.rule: shift to growth-mode proposing capability expansion, test coverage, or documentation tasks
